q: 1. Stadia tacheometry was discovered by James Watt in the year ...............
explain: James Watt is credited with the invention of the stadia system for measuring distances in 1770.

q: 2. The diaphragm of a stadia theodolite is fitted with two additional ...............
explain: A stadia diaphragm has the standard crosshairs plus two additional horizontal 'stadia hairs' (one above and one below the center).

q: 3. The staff intercept will be ...............
options: greater farther off the staff is held
smaller, farther off the staff is held
smaller, nearer the staff is held
same, wherever the staff is held
explain: Due to the divergence of the stadia rays, the intercept (difference between top and bottom hair readings) decreases as the staff moves closer to the instrument.

q: 4. One of the tacheometric constants is additive, the other constant, is ...............
explain: The two tacheometric constants are the multiplying constant (k) and the additive constant (c).

q: 5. Tacheometric formula for horizontal distance using horizontal sights can also suitable be employed for inclined sights through θ by multiplying ...............
options: the multiplying constant by cos²θ and additive constant by cos θ
explain: The standard horizontal distance formula for inclined sights is D = ks cos²θ + c cosθ.

q: 6. The image formed by the objective in the plane of cross hairs is ...............
explain: A simple objective lens in a telescope produces a real and inverted image at the focal plane.

q: 7. The brightness of the image ............... the magnifying power.
options: varies directly as the square of
varies inversely as the square of
explain: Image brightness is inversely proportional to the square of the magnification because the same amount of light is spread over a larger area.

q: 8. The ratio of the focal length of the objective to that of an eye-piece of a telescope is called its ...............
explain: Magnification (m) = f(objective) / f(eyepiece).

q: 9. θ1 and θ2 are the angles of elevation from A to the top and bottom of vertically held rod of length S at B. The horizontal distance AB is ...............
explain: Using trigonometry: h1 = D tan θ1 and h2 = D tan θ2. The length S = h1 - h2 = D(tan θ1 - tan θ2), so D = S/(tan θ1 - tan θ2).

q: 10. Subtense tacheometry is generally preferred to if ground is ...............
explain: The subtense bar method is particularly useful in rough or undulating terrain where chaining is difficult or impossible.

q: 11. In a tacheometer provided with anallactic lens distance between object glass and vertical axis is 15 cm. Focal length of the objective is 15 cm and that of anallactic lens is 10 cm. Hence distance between the two lenses is ...............
explain: For an anallactic lens, the distance between the objective and the anallactic lens (d) is calculated to make the additive constant zero. In this specific configuration, it results in 17.5 cm.

q: 12. The theodolites used for making tacheometric observations by optical wedge system, are ...............
options: provided with stadia hairs in front of eye piece
not provided with stadia hairs at all
fitted with a glass wedge inside the telescope
fitted with a glass wedge in front of telescope
explain: The optical wedge system involves placing a glass wedge in front of half the objective to create a fixed displacement for distance measurement.

q: 13. Tacheometry is best suited
explain: Tacheometric surveying, which avoids the need for chaining altogether, is best suited for broken (rough/undulating) ground where direct chaining would be difficult or impossible.

q: 14. The tacheometric method of contouring is particularly suitable
options: when a contoured map of hill is required
when the area is not very extensive
in surveys of roads or railways
explain: The tacheometric method, which is fast and does not require chaining, is particularly suitable for contouring hilly terrain where direct measurement would be difficult.

q: 15. Substense bar is an instrument used for .............
options: measurement of horizontal distances in plane areas
measurement of horizontal distances in undulated areas
explain: A subtense bar is used in tacheometry to measure horizontal distances indirectly, which is particularly useful in rough or undulating terrain where chaining is difficult.

q: 16. The number of horizontal cross wires in a stadia diaphragm is .............
explain: A stadia diaphragm consists of one central horizontal cross-hair and two additional short horizontal hairs (stadia hairs) placed equidistantly above and below the center.

q: 17. With the help of a Tacheometer we can measure
explain: A tacheometer, essentially a theodolite fitted with stadia hairs, is primarily used to measure vertical angles (along with horizontal angles and stadia readings) to compute distance and elevation.

q: 18. The branch of surveying in which both horizontal and vertical positions of a point, are determined by making in instrumental observations, is known .............
explain: Tacheometry is a branch of angular surveying in which horizontal and vertical distances are determined by optical observations on a staff, eliminating chaining.

q: 19. The ratio of the distances at which a stated length can be distinguished by the telescope and the human eye, respectively, is called .............
explain: Magnification power is the ratio of the size of the image formed on the retina when seen through a telescope to the size of the image when seen by the naked eye.

q: 20. Tacheometry is adopted where
options: too many curves at the borders exists
explain: Tacheometry is ideal for broken or rugged ground where direct measurement with a chain or tape is difficult.

q: 21. The method of tacheometry in which the stadia hair intercept is fixed, is known as
explain: In the fixed hair method, the distance between the stadia hairs is constant, and the staff intercept varies.

q: 22. The stadia hairs are not used in
explain: Tangential tacheometry involves taking two sightings with the central horizontal hair to two different targets on the staff; stadia hairs are not required.

q: 23. The method of tacheometry in which the observation is made with stadia wires with variable interval is known as
explain: In the movable hair (or subtense) method, the distance between hairs is adjusted to read a fixed staff intercept.

q: 24. The number of horizontal cross wires in a stadia diaphragm is
explain: A standard stadia diaphragm has three horizontal wires: the central hair and two stadia hairs (upper and lower).

q: 25. The horizontal distances obtained by tacheometry are corrected for
explain: Because tacheometry involves long-distance optical sightings, errors due to Earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction must be considered.

q: 26. The multiplying constant of a tacheometer is
explain: The multiplying constant (k) is defined as the focal length (f) divided by the stadia interval (i).

q: 27. If a tacheometer is fitted with an anallatic lens
options: additive constant is 100, multiplying constant is zero
multiplying constant is 100, additive constant is zero
both multiplying and additive constants are 100
both multiplying and additive constants are 50
explain: The anallatic lens is a special convex lens fitted in a tacheometer to make the additive constant (f+c) zero, simplifying distance calculations to D = Ks.

q: 28. In tacheometrical observations, vertical staff holding is generally preferred to normal staffing, due to
options: minimum effect of careless holding on the result
explain: Holding the staff vertically is easier for the staff-man and results in smaller errors if the staff is slightly out of plumb compared to trying to hold it normal (perpendicular) to the line of sight.

q: 29. In tangential tacheometry, an ordinary level staff is used
explain: Tangential tacheometry calculations assume the staff is held perfectly vertical so that the tangent values of the observed vertical angles can be applied.

q: 30. Horizontal distances obtained tacheometrically are corrected for
explain: For very long sights, tacheometric readings must be corrected for the earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction, which affect the perceived staff intercept.

q: 31. Tilt of the staff in stadia tacheometry increases the intercept if it is
options: away from the telescope pointing down hill
away from the telescope pointing up-hill
explain: When the staff is tilted away from the telescope while pointing up-hill, the intercept (distance between hairs) appears larger than it would be if held truly vertical.

q: 32. The intercept of a staff
options: is maximum if the staff is held truly normal...
is minimum if the staff is held truly normal...
decreases if the staff is tilted away from normal
increases if the staff is tilted towards normal
explain: The staff intercept is at its mathematical minimum when the staff is held exactly normal (perpendicular) to the line of sight.

q: 33. If vertical angles of inclined sights do not exceed 10° and non-verticality of the staff remains within 1° stadia system...
options: staff normal as well as vertical
explain: For small vertical angles (under 10°), holding the staff vertical is the standard practice in stadia tacheometry as it simplifies the reduction of readings to horizontal distances.

q: 34. The stadia intercept on a fixed hair instrument vertically held is 1 m. if its constraints are 800 and 0.5 and total number of turns are 16, the horizontal distance between the instrument and target is
explain: Using the formula $D = Ks + C$, where $K=100$ and $C=0.5$. If intercept $s=0.5$, then $D = (100 	imes 0.5) + 0.5 = 50.5$ meters.

q: 35. The stadia lines of a tacheometer are .............
explain: Stadia hairs consist of a top horizontal wire and a bottom horizontal wire equidistant from the central horizontal crosshair, used for distance measurement.

q: 36. A branch of surveying in which the horizontal and vertical distances of points are obtained by instrumental observations, is known as .............
explain: Tacheometry allows for the calculation of both horizontal and vertical distances using optical measurements (stadia hairs) rather than tapes/chains.

q: 37. The principle of tacheometry is used .............
options: for filling in detail in topographic surveys
explain: Tacheometry is versatile and used for contouring, topographic mapping, and specialized surveys like hydrography.

q: 38. The multiplying constant for the tacheometer is .............
explain: The multiplying constant is denoted by $k = f/i$, where $f$ is focal length and $i$ is stadia interval.

q: 39. The additive constant for the tacheometer is .............
explain: The additive constant is denoted by $C = f + d$, where $d$ is the distance from the objective to the vertical axis.

q: 40. The multiplying constant for the tacheometer is, generally, kept as .............
explain: To simplify distance calculations ($D = ks + C$), $k$ is almost always set to 100.

q: 41. The value of additive constant for the tacheometer varies from .............
explain: For external focusing telescopes, $f+d$ typically ranges from 30cm to 45cm.

q: 42. The desirable multiplying and additive constants for a tacheometer .............
explain: An ideal tacheometer has a multiplying constant of 100 and an additive constant of 0 (achieved with an anallatic lens).

q: 43. Anallatic lens is provided .............
options: exactly at the line of intersection of vertical and horizontal axes
explain: The anallatic lens is a special convex lens placed between the objective and the diaphragm to simplify calculations.

q: 44. Anallatic lens is provided to .............
options: nullify both the constants of tacheometer
make multiplying constant as 100 and additive constant as zero
explain: The primary purpose of an anallatic lens is to make the additive constant ($f+d$) zero, allowing the distance to be calculated simply as $D = ks$.

q: 45. Anallatic lens is a .............
explain: The anallatic lens used in tacheometers is a convex lens.

q: 46. Tacheometry is best suited .............
explain: Broken or undulating ground makes traditional chaining highly inaccurate and labor-intensive, whereas tacheometry handles it easily using optical sights.
